Tirksliai, Mazeikiai New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Telšių apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. This cemetery was originally established as a burial place for the Jews of Tirksliai, a small town four miles from Mazeikiai; once Mazeikiai's own Jewish community formed and grew rapidly following the arrival of the railway, local Jews began burying their dead here too. On August 3, 1941, all of Mazeikiai's Jewish men were led to prepared pits near this very cemetery and shot; women and children were murdered in the same pits on August 9. In total, around 4,000 Jews from Mazeikiai and the surrounding area were shot dead here in August 1941 — this is the site directly behind the massacre repeatedly referenced at numerous other towns documented elsewhere in this collection, including Seda, Klykoliai, Laizuva, Leckava, Mosedis, Pasvitinys, and Pikeliai, whose Jews were all brought here to die. During the Soviet years, the old cemetery was destroyed and most of its tombstones taken away.
